color grade with green and red magic glow, shallow depth of field, high-detail 
film look, fast dynamic camera.

[0–1s] Ultra-wide fisheye shot of a gothic castle resembling Big Ben and the

prompt:

Do not transfer the reference background, pose, camera angle or lighting. Keep the same recognizable cake design throughout the video.

@image2 = vehicle identity only. Preserve the vehicle’s recognizable body shape, proportions, paint color, wheel design, lighting elements and distinctive exterior features: a metallic pink-lavender luxury grand tourer with a tall vertical-slat rose-gold grille, round headlights, intricate rose-gold multi-spoke wheels, and glittering translucent butterfly-wing doors with rose-gold veining. Do not transfer the reference background, pose, camera angle or lighting. Keep the same recognizable vehicle design throughout the entire video with no morphing.

@image3 = subject identity only. Preserve the recognizable face, facial structure, eyes, skin tone, hair and apparent age of the subject shown in @image3. Do not transfer the reference background, pose, camera angle or lighting. Keep the same recognizable subject throughout the video from every visible angle. The prompt must work equally well for any subject provided in @image3, regardless of gender.

FORMAT: 16:9 widescreen, 15 seconds total, single continuous take.

SCENE

First-person POV shot outdoors in a wide open space (empty paved plaza at golden hour, soft hazy skyline far in the distance), filmed as one continuous take.

The unseen POV person stands still, holding the birthday cake from @image1 close to the camera in the foreground. The cake is supported naturally in the POV hands and stays visible for most of the shot. The cake has many small lit candles, all clearly burning with warm flickering flames.

From the distance, the vehicle from @image2 rushes toward the camera at high speed and enters a dramatic controlled drift with visible sideways motion, tire slip and light tire smoke.

The subject from @image3 leans halfway out of the driver-side front window of the moving vehicle, upper body outside the window, clearly visible during the drift.

ACTION

0.0–2.0s: First-person POV. The birthday cake from @image1 with many lit candles fills the lower foreground, held steady. In the distance, the vehicle from @image2 appears and accelerates rapidly toward the camera.

2.0–9.0s: As the vehicle begins its fast drifting approach, the motion enters cinematic slow motion. The vehicle does not brake or pause. It keeps moving fast in one smooth, controlled drifting arc toward the POV, sliding sideways, with tire smoke and glinting light on the butterfly-wing doors. The subject from @image3 is already leaning halfway out of the driver-side window, facing the cake and camera.

9.0–11.5s: At the closest point of the drifting slow-motion pass, the subject leans further outward and blows toward the cake from @image1. The blow clearly extinguishes the candles: flames bend, flicker and go out as a direct result of the breath, with thin wisps of smoke rising.

11.5–15.0s: At the strongest visual peak (vehicle closest, subject extended from the window, candles just extinguished), cut to a dramatic high-contrast black-and-white freeze frame. Hold the frozen frame until the end of the video (about 3 seconds). Do not continue with the vehicle driving away.

CAMERA

First-person POV only, as if seen through the eyes of the unseen cake-holder. The camera stays in one position with only subtle natural body movement. No cuts, no angle changes, no third-person shots, no drone view. The cake from @image1 stays in the foreground. The final frame is a locked black-and-white still.

AUDIO / MUSIC

Background music: a cinematic, stylish, slow-building track. Start with a soft, dreamy bass-driven synth pulse with light chimes (a hint of music-box sparkle to match the birthday theme) over distant engine and tire sounds. As the car nears and slow motion begins, shift into a deep, heartbeat-like low-end with a rising synth swell and filtered, slowed-down beat. Layer synchronized Foley over the music: tire screech during the drift, engine rumble, and one clear human breath at the moment of blowing, with a soft candle-snuff sound. At the freeze frame, cut the music on a single deep bass hit, then let a soft reverb tail fade out cleanly. No vocals, no dialogue.

CONSTRAINTS

Single continuous take, no cuts, first-person POV only. The cake in the foreground must match @image1 in overall appearance and candle arrangement. The vehicle must approach at high speed and perform a close, controlled drift pass near the POV. The movement must feel stylish, fast and controlled, not like the car is stopping in front of the POV holder. Do not show the vehicle braking, pausing or slowing awkwardly before the closest pass. Slow motion must begin during the fast drifting approach, while the vehicle is still closing distance, not after it has nearly stopped. The subject must be leaning halfway out of the driver-side front window, clearly visible throughout the drift, and must blow out the candles during the closest pass. The candles go out only as a direct result of the blowing. End at the climax with a black-and-white freeze frame held for about 3 seconds, with no drive-away ending. Do not add extra people. Do not change the cake design, vehicle design or subject identity.

prompt:
Create a highly realistic 30-second cinematic historical sequence set in Korea during the 1950s. The entire video should feel like a naturally observed fragment of ordinary life from that era — not a vlog, not a modern recording, and not a person performing for a camera.

MAIN SUBJECT:
A young Korean woman in her early 20s with a consistent, natural appearance and believable facial features. She has black hair tied loosely back, minimal makeup, natural skin texture and subtle everyday expressions.

Her outfit is period-inspired but youthful and attractive: a fitted cropped short-sleeve cotton top paired with high-waisted shorts ending around the upper thigh, simple flat leather shoes, and a small understated necklace. The clothing should look like authentic, practical 1950s cotton clothing rather than modern fashion. Natural fabric wrinkles, slightly faded colors and realistic stitching.

CONCEPT:
Show several small moments from her ordinary daily routine, progressing naturally from inside her home to the neighborhood outside. She never looks into or acknowledges the camera. There is no visible camera, filming equipment, phone or modern recording device.

SCENE 1 — MORNING AT HOME | 0–6 SEC
Inside a modest 1950s Korean home with wooden floors, simple bedding, handmade household objects and sunlight entering through a paper-covered window.

The woman folds a small stack of freshly washed clothes, then carries them outside in a woven basket. Her movements are casual and unhurried. Sunlight falls naturally across the room, revealing dust particles in the air.

SCENE 2 — HANGING LAUNDRY | 6–11 SEC
She steps into a small courtyard behind the house and hangs clothes on a simple rope line.

Show her stretching upward to place a shirt over the line, securing it with simple wooden clothespins, then smoothing another garment with her hands. A light breeze gently moves the hanging clothes and her loose hair.

Include small environmental details: clay pots, wooden walls, stone ground, a water basin and neighboring rooftops in the background.

SCENE 3 — PREPARING TO GO OUT | 11–16 SEC
She returns inside and quickly prepares to leave. She picks up a small woven shoulder bag, checks herself naturally in a small old-fashioned mirror, adjusts her hair and puts on her simple shoes.

Her expression is relaxed and spontaneous — never posed.

SCENE 4 — WALKING THROUGH THE NEIGHBORHOOD | 16–22 SEC
She walks out through a wooden gate into a quiet 1950s Korean residential lane.

Show traditional houses, stone walls, bicycles, wooden carts, laundry lines, children playing farther away and neighbors performing ordinary chores. She walks naturally through the scene carrying her small bag.

SCENE 5 — EVERYDAY ERRAND | 22–27 SEC
She approaches a small public water pump or communal washing area. She briefly fills a small metal container, adjusts her grip and continues walking.

Keep the interaction simple and believable. No vendor, no market performance and no staged interaction.

SCENE 6 — FINAL MOMENT | 27–30 SEC
She walks along a sunlit lane bordered by old Korean houses and trees. A breeze moves her clothes naturally as she passes through patches of sunlight and shadow.

She briefly pauses to look toward something happening farther down the street, smiles subtly, then continues walking out of frame.

VISUAL STYLE:
Authentic 1950s Korean period-film aesthetic. Photorealistic historical reconstruction with soft natural daylight, slightly faded monochrome or extremely subtle muted color, fine analog film grain, gentle halation, slight lens softness, natural exposure fluctuations and occasional tiny imperfections characteristic of period film.

The image must NOT look like a modern video with a generic "vintage filter." Architecture, clothing, props, materials and human behavior should all convincingly belong to 1950s Korea.

CAMERA:
Observational period cinematography. The camera exists as an unseen observer rather than a participant. Use carefully composed static shots mixed with very slow natural camera movement. No handheld vlog movement, no selfie perspective, no modern stabilization, no dramatic zooms and no shots where the subject appears aware of being filmed.

AUDIO:
Pure environmental sound: birds, distant voices, footsteps, fabric moving in the breeze, wooden doors, water flowing from the pump, distant bicycles and neighborhood activity. No music, no narration, no modern sound effects.

REALISM:
Every movement must obey real-world physics. Natural hands and fingers, realistic walking, believable fabric deformation, consistent shadows, physically accurate sunlight, authentic facial expressions and continuous character identity. No extra fingers, warped hands, floating objects, distorted faces, modern objects or AI-looking motion.

The final result should feel like a genuine 30-second fragment of everyday Korean life from the 1950s — intimate, quiet, observational and historically believable, with the woman's ordinary routine providing the visual story.

30 seconds, Seedance 2.5, 16:9, ultra-high-quality photorealism, cinematic historical realism, consistent character identity, coherent transitions, natural motion and authentic 1950s Korean atmosphere.

title: The Dark Knight Rises — LA helicopter motorcycle pursuit
prompt:
SEEDANCE 2.5 — LOS ANGELES HELICOPTER MOTORCYCLE PURSUIT

Duration: 30 seconds
Aspect ratio: 16:9 widescreen
Frame rate: 24 fps
Visual style: Ultra-realistic viral helicopter pursuit footage, raw local-news / eyewitness recording, unpolished documentary realism.
CORE VISUAL CONCEPT
A chaotic, high-stakes police pursuit filmed entirely from a single helicopter-mounted aerial camera above Los Angeles in bright California daylight. The footage feels like an unexpected live-news incident captured by an experienced but struggling camera operator. The result must look like authentic broadcast footage, not a polished action movie.
Harsh midday sunlight, hard-edged shadows, heat shimmer rising from asphalt, dusty concrete, palm-lined streets, freeway interchanges, industrial blocks, parking lots, overpasses, and a wide concrete flood-control channel. Distant downtown Los Angeles appears through atmospheric haze.

Camera characteristics: Long-lens aerial footage, natural helicopter vibration, irregular handheld-style corrections, abrupt optical zooms, occasional focus hunting, imperfect framing, brief tracking errors, compression artifacts, realistic motion blur, and rapid but physically plausible pans. The camera must feel heavy and airborne, with delayed reactions when changing direction.

CHARACTER AND VEHICLE CONTINUITY

Main subject: The exact same motorcycle rider represented @image1 riding the exact same heavy motorcycle @image2.

Treat all supplied material references as visual references. Preserve the rider’s identity, clothing, body proportions, motorcycle silhouette, paint, colors, mechanical details, and overall scale. Do not redesign or replace either subject between shots.

The rider is highly skilled, aggressive, and controlled, leaning naturally through turns, absorbing landings with realistic suspension compression, and maintaining convincing balance at high speed.

Multiple police vehicles pursue him in the background. Maintain consistent vehicle appearance and believable road positions.

SHOT-BY-SHOT TIMELINE

00:00–00:05 — IMMEDIATE VIRAL HOOK

The helicopter camera is already searching frantically over a busy Los Angeles boulevard. Suddenly, the motorcycle rider blasts into frame between moving police cars. The camera operator snaps into a fast optical zoom, briefly overshoots, and corrects the framing.

The rider cuts sharply across the edge of a parking lot, jumps a low curb, and disappears momentarily behind palm trees before reappearing. A brief close aerial zoom catches the spinning rear wheel, visible tire rotation, and suspension movement as the motorcycle accelerates away.

Police sirens begin overlapping with the deep, throaty motorcycle engine. Strong helicopter rotor vibration is audible throughout.

00:05–00:10 — CHAOTIC PURSUIT

The rider rejoins the boulevard and threads through moving traffic, narrowly passing between vehicles before veering up a sloped driveway. He launches over a low concrete divider in one clean, controlled jump.

Several police cars follow on the roadway, their red-and-blue lights flashing in the harsh sunlight and their sirens echoing between buildings.

The helicopter camera over-zooms and briefly loses the motorcycle behind roadside structures. The operator rapidly pans back and reacquires the rider just as both wheels land. Show believable suspension compression, tire contact, and immediate forward acceleration.

00:10–00:15 — FLOOD CHANNEL REVEAL

The motorcycle enters a sloped service access and drops into a vast concrete flood-control channel. The helicopter camera pulls back into a wide aerial reveal, exposing the channel’s enormous scale, angled concrete banks, drainage seams, and distant bridges.

The rider accelerates along the channel floor, leaving a faint trail of dust and road grit. The helicopter banks to maintain visual contact, and the camera tilts steeply downward.

The operator then punches in toward the motorcycle’s rear wheel and suspension as the bike races along the concrete surface. Deep engine noise echoes naturally through the channel.

00:15–00:20 — WALL-RIDE STUNT

The rider suddenly steers up the angled concrete channel wall, climbing diagonally while maintaining realistic tire contact and body positioning. He holds a dramatic high line for a brief moment before descending smoothly toward the flat channel floor.

The helicopter banks hard to follow the maneuver. The long-lens camera shakes and briefly loses the rider near the edge of the frame before recovering him.

The motorcycle’s engine pitch rises under acceleration, then changes as the rider descends and regains the channel floor. Police radio chatter becomes more active, with clipped, overlapping transmissions from the pursuing units.

00:20–00:25 — UNEXPECTED ESCAPE ROUTE

The rider exits through a sloped service ramp and crosses beneath a broad concrete overpass. The helicopter camera continues tracking along the original trajectory, but the motorcycle unexpectedly emerges on a parallel industrial access road.

The camera operator reacts late, swings rapidly across the overpass, and catches the rider accelerating over a natural rise in the road. The motorcycle launches into a long, clean jump in full California daylight.

Capture the complete silhouette against the bright sky, with the rider maintaining a compact, stable posture. The bike follows a believable ballistic arc, with realistic forward momentum and gravity. The helicopter camera zooms in during the jump but struggles to keep the entire motorcycle inside the frame.

00:25–00:30 — ICONIC DISAPPEARANCE

The motorcycle lands on the industrial road with a firm suspension compression and continues accelerating toward another overpass. A quick zoom catches the spinning rear wheel as the rider rushes into the deep shadow underneath.

The helicopter camera overshoots the entrance, then circles and searches across the surrounding roads, concrete structures, and industrial blocks. The rider cannot be found.

Over the helicopter’s radio, an adult male reporter says in a stunned, restrained voice:

“We just lost him.”

The helicopter continues a shaky, wide aerial search over Los Angeles. Police sirens fade into the distance while the helicopter engine and rotor thump remain prominent.

Hard cut to black at exactly 30 seconds.

SOUND DESIGN — CRITICAL

Create a continuous, layered, realistic location-audio mix. Avoid artificial action-movie sound effects.

Motorcycle: Deep, throaty, realistic heavy-motorcycle engine with changing RPM, aggressive acceleration, throttle blips, gear changes, and Doppler shifts as the rider moves relative to the helicopter.

Police vehicles: Authentic emergency-vehicle sirens, shifting in volume and pitch with distance, mixed with faint tire noise and engine sounds.

Helicopter: Constant rotor thump, turbine whine, airframe vibration, and subtle wind buffeting the onboard microphone.

Police radio: Realistic, narrow-band radio transmissions with static, brief squelch bursts, clipped speech, overlapping dispatch and pursuing-unit communication, and occasional unintelligible background chatter. The voices should sound as though they originate inside the helicopter or through its radio equipment.
Environment: Los Angeles traffic ambience, distant horns, freeway noise, and natural echoes inside the concrete flood channel.
Reporter: One brief, clear male spoken line at the end: “We just lost him.” No narration over the stunts.
Maintain a believable audio perspective. The motorcycle engine should become louder as the rider approaches the camera’s tracking area and quieter as he disappears into the distance. Do not let the engine sound unnaturally close during wide aerial shots.
REALISM AND MOTION CONSTRAINTS
One continuous helicopter-based observational perspective, with no ground-level camera cuts, drone shots, third-person chase angles, or impossible camera teleportation. Natural reframing and optical zoom changes are allowed.

Maintain consistent rider and motorcycle identity across all 30 seconds. All stunts must remain readable, with physically plausible motorcycle traction, suspension travel, acceleration, takeoff, airtime, and landing.

The helicopter must follow plausible aerial trajectories and cannot instantly change position. Maintain recognizable Los Angeles urban geography and consistent daylight direction.

Negative prompt: Cinematic color grading, glossy blockbuster visuals, artificial slow motion, impossible motorcycle physics, floating wheels, distorted motorcycle geometry, duplicate riders, changing outfits, changing bike design, warped police vehicles, teleportation, excessive motion blur, exaggerated explosions, crashes, gore, readable text, watermarks, visible brand logos, and artificial or repetitive sound effects.

author: alessia_orbit
title: Pandora's Box Was a Jar — Lid Stays On
prompt:
Lock the room with a photo, not words.

Five storyboards, five different rooms. I described the same Paris atelier in words every time, and every run built a new studio. One reference photo of the room fixed it on the next try, light included.

Only in the storyboard, though. In the video, that wide room photo drags every close-up back into a wide shot, so the video gets the room in words only.

Seedance 2.5 · 1 render · ~$3.20

Prompt 👇

[STYLE + CAMERA + ATMOSPHERE]
20-second, 16:9 landscape, hyper-realistic live-action short. A 24-year-old woman builds a tall clay storage jar by hand in a grand old artist's atelier in Paris: she slams and wedges terracotta-red clay, throws a base on an old potter's wheel, builds the walls up with heavy ropes of clay, beats them into shape with a wooden paddle, and finishes the rim. A montage of one continuous pottery session at real-time speed: eight shots, each hard cut jumping forward in time so the jar is visibly more complete in every shot where it appears, smears of red clay building up on her hands and forearms as it goes. Handheld documentary feel, filmed as if by chance: slightly imperfect framing, subtle handheld drift, gentle exposure breathing, autofocus arriving half a beat late. Each shot is one steady handheld framing with only a gentle drift, and every shot has its own camera position and its own body position; the one camera move is a slow push toward her eyes in the seventh shot. Real-time the whole way, never slow motion.
Lighting: soft overcast daylight through the single tall window as the only light source, brightest near the window and falling off gradually darker toward the foreground and the corners, gentle side falloff with smooth tonal transitions across her face, her body and the clay, bright and airy but with real directional shadow, never flat dead light. No studio beauty light, no god-ray beams, no sunbeams, no rim light, no added lamps. Face shadows stay soft but present, do not over-fill.

LOCKED SET:
- The room: a grand, very tall old 19th-century atelier, weathered ochre-beige limestone and plaster walls curving into shallow apse corners, a vaulted ceiling with faint faded painted decoration, a single very tall white-framed rectangular French casement window in the middle of the far wall, rows of white plaster busts on pedestals along both side walls, a long rough wooden trestle work table on the right, pale worn stone floor. Aged, lived-in, grand but working, never a clean empty film set.
- THE POTTERY CORNER: an old heavy potter's wheel stands on the open stone floor in the left-center of the room, between the left row of busts and the window: a wide round flat metal wheel head on a squat round drum base about knee height, crusted with dried red clay, with a low sturdy wooden stool about knee high beside it. She slams the clay at the long trestle work table on the right; on it lie a bucket of water, a sponge, a flat wooden paddle, a smooth round grey stone, a thin curved wooden rib and a cutting wire. The only pottery anywhere in the room is her one jar.
- DIRECTION LOCK: the wheel and the jar are always on frame-LEFT of her body and she works facing frame-LEFT, except in the seventh shot, where the camera faces her across the jar. The camera is always in front of her or at her side. The 180-degree line held, the space never flipping between cuts.

LOCKED CAST:
- THE WOMAN: Use @character as her locked visual identity, an adult woman, age 24 - preserve her face, low bun, body proportions and outfit exactly across every shot, never reinterpret or let her face turn generic. Matte natural skin, real pores and fine peach-fuzz. Warm chestnut brown hair in a low bun at the nape, a few loose face-framing strands at the cheeks. Outfit, identical every frame: a fitted plain white short cropped t-shirt sitting high above the waist leaving the midriff bare, the thin soft stretch-knit clinging with real fabric creases across the bust and waist, short sleeves, plain crew neckline; relaxed loose dark charcoal grey trousers on the hips, no branding; plain white low sneakers. Smears of terracotta-red clay on her hands and forearms only, building up shot by shot; the white tee, the trousers and her face stay clean. She is the only person ever seen. Calm, absorbed, focused on the clay throughout, never posing, never looking at the lens, her figure seen only through the natural slam, lift, lean, reach and stretch of the work.
- THE CLAY: coarse terracotta-red clay, the iron-rich red earthenware of ancient Greek storage jars; wet it is a deep brick red, and as it firms up it turns a slightly paler, matte red.
- THE JAR, her own work: ONE single large storage jar in the shape of an ancient Greek pithos, plain terracotta-red clay with faint horizontal throwing rings, no decoration, no handles, no figures, no faces. The same jar, the same color and the same width of belly in every shot; only its stage advances: no jar yet in the first two shots, then a short squat open base, then low open walls about knee high, then tall to her chest with a swelling belly and a straight open top, then almost full height with the shoulders curving in, then finished with a wide mouth and a heavy rolled rim, standing on the wheel about as high as her shoulder, and at the very end closed with a flat round lid of the same red clay.

AUDIO:
All sound captured in-camera by a single handheld camera, raw, never a studio mix, never dubbed. Her quiet breathing, one heavy wet thud as the clay block slams onto the wooden table, a dull wet thump as the clay ball lands on the wheel head, the low steady rumble of the turning wheel, the soft wet squelch of clay under her fingers, a few dull flat knocks of the wooden paddle on the firm clay wall, the faint scrape of the wooden rib along the rim, a soft dull tap of the clay lid settling, the faint room tone of a large stone hall, distant muffled street sound beyond the window. No dialogue, no music, no BGM, no added effect sound, everything kept low and real.

[IMAGE REFERENCES]
@character = the woman: face, hair, body and outfit. The only face in the video.
The clip BEGINS already mid-motion.

[TIMELINE]
0-2.5s | CLOSE THREE-QUARTER FRONT FROM SLIGHTLY ABOVE, SLAMMING THE CLAY: camera very close and a little above her, in front of her, looking down at her bowed head and leaning body, framed from the top of her head to her waist, already mid-motion. At the long trestle table she lifts a heavy block of wet red clay a little off the tabletop with both hands and slams it straight down with real weight: one heavy wet thud, the block squashing flat at frame-LEFT of her body, a few flecks of clay jumping off it. Both hands stay pressed on it, arms straight, her whole upper body following through forward and down toward the camera, the white tee stretching across her as she leans in. Her head bowed, eyelids lowered, her gaze on the clay, never up at the lens. The edge of the table and the clay sit in the near foreground at frame-LEFT, cut off by the frame edge.
2.5-5s | VERY LOW ANGLE BACKLIT SIDE, LIFTING THE CLAY BALL OVER THE WHEEL: camera just above the floor, close, at her left side, looking up, framed from her hips up, her body filling most of the frame height, the tall bright window directly behind her. She stands beside the bare wheel side-on in profile facing frame-LEFT, her left side toward the camera, and raises a round wedged ball of red clay, as big as a melon, with both hands up to the height of her head, then throws it hard down onto the center of the bare wheel head below her at frame-LEFT with a dull wet thump. The bright window glows directly behind her so her lifted arms, the long stretched line of her torso, her bare midriff, narrow waist and the curve into her hips read as a clean outline against the light. Her face in profile, eyes on the clay ball, face shadows soft but readable.
5-7.5s | TIGHT CLOSE on her face and hands together, eye level, side-front angle, framed from the top of her head to her chest, her face filling the upper half of the frame: she sits on the low stool bent low over the spinning wheel, and along the bottom edge of the frame, just below her chin, her fingers are inside the short squat open base of red clay, opening it out, her elbows held out to the sides, wet red clay on her fingers and wrists. Her whole face stays clear above her hands, eyes down on the clay, jaw set in concentration. Behind her, soft and out of focus, the weathered ochre wall and a white plaster bust. Her face large and sharp.
7.5-10s | LOW PURE SIDE PROFILE AT WHEEL HEIGHT, ASTRIDE THE WHEEL: camera at the height of the wheel head, close, at her exact left side, perpendicular to her body, framed from the wheel head up to just above her head, her body filling most of the frame height, white busts soft behind her. She sits astride the wheel on the low stool, one leg on each side of the drum base, facing frame-LEFT, the drum base and the wheel head hiding her lap. The jar's low open walls, now about knee high, turn on the wheel in front of her. She leans far forward toward frame-LEFT over them, both arms extended, laying a heavy rope of red clay around the top and pressing it down with both hands, the forward reach stretching her torso so her chest, narrow waist and the curve of her hip on the stool read as one long unbroken side line. Her face in profile, lowered to the clay.
10-12.5s | THREE-QUARTER FRONT AT WAIST HEIGHT, BEATING THE WALL WITH THE PADDLE: camera at her waist height, three-quarter in front of her, framed from mid-thigh up to just above her head. The jar stands on the wheel at frame-LEFT of her body, now tall to about her chest but still unfinished: its lower half swells into a round belly, its top is still a straight open wall with no rim, its clay firm, matte and slightly paler. She stands close against it facing frame-LEFT: her LEFT arm reaches over the open top and down inside the jar up to the elbow, her left hand holding the smooth round grey stone against the inside of the wall, and her RIGHT hand swings the flat wooden paddle against the outside of the wall at the same spot, two or three firm slaps with dull flat knocks. She leans in so close that the front of her white tee lightly touches the firm, dry outer wall, just a light touch, nothing pressed flat. Her face three-quarter to the camera, eyes on the spot she is beating.
12.5-15s | LOW ANGLE SIDE, STANDING ON THE STOOL AGAINST THE BRIGHT WINDOW: camera low near the floor at her exact left side, perpendicular to her body, looking up, framed from her feet on the stool up to just above her head, her whole body in frame, the tall bright window directly behind her. The jar on the wheel at frame-LEFT is almost full height, its shoulders curving in. She stands up on the low stool facing frame-LEFT and bends forward from the hips over the jar's mouth, her RIGHT arm reaching all the way down inside the jar up to the shoulder, smoothing the bottom inside, her LEFT hand resting flat on the jar's shoulder. Her whole body is one long side line from her feet on the stool through her legs, hips, narrow waist and bent back to her head, drawn as a clean silhouette against the glowing window. The camera sees her from her left side: her face and the front of her body side-on to the camera, her back turned away from it. Her face in profile, cheek just above the rim, eyes looking down into the jar.
15-17.5s | ACROSS THE RIM AT HER FACE: the jar is finished now, a wide mouth with a heavy rolled rim. The camera sits just beyond the jar at the height of the rim, facing her across its open mouth: the curve of the wet red rim runs through the near foreground, soft and out of focus. She stands on the low stool on the far side of the jar, facing the camera, framed from the top of her head down to her chest. Her RIGHT hand holds the thin curved wooden rib against the outside of the rim and her LEFT fingertips rest just inside it, shaping the lip as it slowly turns, her hands low at the rim so her whole face is clear above them. The camera pushes slowly forward across the rim toward her face, focus settling sharp on her eyes. Calm, a light quiet concentration, eyes on the lip of the jar, never the lens.
17.5-20s | WIDE full pull-back from the near end of the room, camera at standing eye level looking straight at the window wall, the whole atelier visible from floor to vault, the tall window behind throwing the room into soft backlit depth: the wheel stands on the open stone floor in the left-center with the finished tall red jar on it, now closed with its flat round red clay lid, still wet and untouched. She has stepped two paces away from it, to its right and a little closer to the window, so the tall bright window glows directly behind her, small in the frame. She stands side-on in profile facing frame-LEFT toward her jar, her hands empty and nowhere near the jar, and slowly raises both arms high above her head in one long stretch, fingers interlacing, palms turning up toward the vault, her back gently arching, her chin tipping up, her eyes closing, one long quiet exhale at the end of a long day's work. The window light draws her raised arms, the long line of her torso, her bare midriff, narrow waist and the curve into her hips as one clean silhouette. The short tee lifts a little with the stretch and still covers her ribs. She holds the stretch at the top, still, never looking at the lens. Against the far left wall, beside a white plaster bust, a finished strung yew longbow leans upright, untouched and far from her, simply part of the room. Hold this wide as the final frame.

[STYLE & QUALITY BOOSTERS]
Raw handheld documentary atelier footage, 16:9, eight hard jump cuts forward in time, real-time. The same single jar growing only more complete, the same wheel, stool and trestle table, the same outfit and low bun in every shot, a different camera position and a different body position in every shot. Identity lock to @character. Soft window daylight, mild grain.

Avoid: subtitles, text, watermark, anime, 3D-CG, plastic skin, over-beautifying, a second person, more than one jar, a changing jar color, the work flipping sides, her back to the camera, posing for camera, nipple protrusion, clay on her clothes, slow motion, speed ramp, freeze, dramatic god-ray beams, studio beauty light, music, BGM, crowd, commentary.

author: tokyo_Valentine
title: Shibuya Scramble Mech Skull vs Skeletal King
prompt:
Create a 15-second, 16:9 cinematic action video set at Shibuya Scramble Crossing, Tokyo, at night.

CHARACTER REFERENCES
Use only the two character reference images for identity and design.
Reference 1: Character A, the yellow-and-black mechanical skull cyborg.
Reference 2: Character B, the towering skeletal king wearing crimson robes.

A: Approximately 180 cm tall. Chipped yellow industrial armor, horizontal pointed head extensions, skull mask, black breathing hoses, intricate mechanical joints, spiked shoulders, chains, and torn dark fabric.
B: Approximately 260 cm tall. Huge branching black antlers, ornate crown, glowing red eyes, exposed skeletal ribcage, elaborate tattered crimson robes, and an ornate staff.

Preserve their exact silhouettes, proportions, materials, colors, and accessories. Create fluid full-body combat animation and dynamic camera movement. Maintain their height difference.

VISUAL STYLE
Photorealistic live-action cinematography, spectacular destruction VFX, and explosive shonen battle intensity.

Extreme acceleration, brutal close-range punches, powerful blocks, violent recoil, and physical impacts that destroy roads and buildings.

Combine tactile physical realism with aggressive digital corruption: RGB separation, horizontal signal tearing, datamoshing trails, pixel fragmentation, scanline interference, and dirty electronic noise.
Keep the choreography and decisive impacts clearly readable.

GLITCH AND NOISE DIRECTION
Make the effects react to the action.

On punch contact: short, violent RGB displacement around the fighters, horizontal image shearing, and a burst of coarse digital static radiating from the impact.

During extreme acceleration: stretched datamoshing trails and fragmented afterimages attached to moving limbs. These are visual motion trails, not separate characters.

Around the reality fracture: unstable scanlines, displaced image strips, crawling pixel noise, and flickering red-white edges.
During mist transformation: mechanical surfaces break into tiny yellow particles, black vapor, and granular signal noise. The transition remains continuous and visibly follows the body.

During the final destruction: physical fragments mix with pixel breakup, corrupted motion trails, and a dense burst of electronic interference.

Use the strongest corruption in brief bursts, followed by clear moving imagery. Keep physical motion flowing through every effect. Avoid prolonged freezes or static poses.

LOCATION
An empty, rain-soaked Shibuya Scramble Crossing. Recognizable diagonal zebra crossings, giant LED billboards, QFRONT-style architecture, and surrounding shopping towers.

Wet asphalt reflects cold city lights, yellow sparks, and crimson energy.

Billboards briefly malfunction in response to nearby shockwaves: distorted footage, broken scanlines, and signal noise.

Keep the fight within this intersection. Environmental damage accumulates and remains visible.

0–3 SECONDS — EXPLOSIVE COLLISION
Begin immediately in motion.
An ultra-low camera races along the white crossing stripes as both fighters launch toward each other.

A’s fist crashes into B’s blocking forearm. Show clear contact and recoil, followed by an expanding pressure ring that blasts rainwater outward and fractures the asphalt.

At contact, deliver a sharp burst of RGB separation and horizontal signal tearing. Restore a clear image immediately as the movement continues.

Whip-pan into a side-on tracking shot. A drives a heavy punch into B’s guarded ribs.

B slides backward, tearing trenches through the road. The shockwave lifts asphalt slabs and bursts a nearby empty building’s glass facade.
Debris travels outward from the strike. Yellow motion trails and fragmented crimson afterimages emphasize their opposing momentum.

3–5 SECONDS — REALITY FRACTURE
B plants its foot, pivots, and swings its staff in a savage diagonal counterattack.

A crimson energy slash cuts across the viewer’s image plane, opening a glowing fracture through reality directly in front of A.

Shoot from an extreme low Dutch angle as the staff passes close to the lens.

Along the fracture, image strips slide out of alignment. Red-white pixels crawl across the edges. Horizontal static and displaced scanlines expose a narrow black slit.

A ducks beneath the slash.

The camera pushes toward A’s articulated metal hand as it catches the fractured edge and pulls the moving image open like a curtain.

This is a fracture in reality at the camera plane, not a broken billboard or ordinary glass.
5–8 SECONDS — BODY BECOMES MIST
Without pausing, A transforms its entire body into dense black industrial mist threaded with yellow sparks and tiny metal particles.

Feet and legs dissolve first, followed by torso and arms. Its skull and reaching hand disappear last.

Mechanical surfaces progressively fragment into smoky particles and granular digital noise. Show the physical anatomy continuously becoming vapor.

A’s former position becomes completely empty.

The mist flows through the opened fracture.

Rise into an overhead view of Shibuya’s diagonal crossings. Follow one coherent ribbon of black-and-yellow mist racing around B’s blind side and converging directly behind the king.

Use streaming pixel trails and localized datamoshing within the moving vapor. Keep its path and destination obvious.

8–10 SECONDS — REASSEMBLY AND COMBINATION
Dive into a low rear three-quarter angle behind B’s whipping crimson cape.
The mist converges and reconstructs A behind the king. Yellow particles condense into the original skull, armor, arms, and legs.

Digital noise contracts into the mechanical surfaces and disappears as each part becomes solid.

A immediately attacks. B pivots toward the movement.

From over A’s yellow shoulder, show a left body punch connecting with B’s ribs, followed by a compact elbow that snaps the king’s upper body sideways.

Each contact creates a brief pulse of image displacement, metallic sparks, and dirty static. Keep the connecting fist, cracking bone, and recoil visible.

Arc toward a clear three-quarter side angle as A plants its foot and draws back its right fist.

10–13 SECONDS — FINAL PUNCH AND COMPLETE DESTRUCTION
A steps forward and drives one decisive rising right straight into B’s sternum.

Show unmistakable fist-to-bone contact from a powerful low angle.
Use a fraction of a second of slow motion at contact, then accelerate into explosive destruction.

A concentrated glitch pulse erupts from the contact point: RGB channels split outward, the surrounding image briefly shears horizontally, and coarse electronic noise follows the expanding shockwave.

B’s ribcage caves inward and shatters outward.

Cracks race through its spine, skull, crown, antlers, arms, and legs. The entire skeletal king physically breaks into thousands of small fragments and fine powder.

Its staff splinters. Its crimson robes tear into scattered scraps.

Mix the flying physical fragments with brief pixel breakup and corrupted motion trails. Show the destruction clearly; the king must visibly shatter rather than simply disappear.

The same impact creates a massive radial shockwave across Shibuya. Asphalt buckles into a crater. Crossing slabs erupt. Nearby empty building facades collapse, and billboard supports bend and fall.

A remains solid and intact through the follow-through.
13–15 SECONDS — AFTERMATH
Pull back into a ground-level wide shot of the devastated intersection.

A stands alone in the crater, slowly lowering its fist as rain and dust move through the damaged city lights.

Only tiny bone chips, snapped antler fragments, broken crown pieces, and torn crimson cloth remain of B.

The king is completely pulverized. No intact skull, body, crown, or antlers remain. It does not regenerate.

Let the aggressive digital interference decay into faint grain and residual noise on damaged billboards.

Finish with a slow camera drift around A’s yellow-and-black silhouette while debris settles around its feet.

CAMERA
Use ground-level tracking, extreme low angles, a hand close-up, an overhead reveal, an over-the-shoulder attack, and a clear final impact angle.

Connect cuts through movement and preserve spatial continuity.

Use selective motion blur during acceleration, crisp silhouettes at contact, and camera shake precisely on impact.

SOUND
Heavy metallic punches, sharp bone fractures, tearing digital distortion, rushing mist, deep shockwaves, collapsing concrete, and raining glass.

Synchronize short bitcrushed crackles and electronic noise with the glitch bursts.
Build aggressive industrial percussion through the fight. Drop the music at the final punch, exposing the impact and destruction. Finish with rain, settling debris, and fading electrical interference.

FINAL REQUIREMENTS
Full-screen 16:9 moving cinematic video.
No dialogue, subtitles, added titles, or watermarks.
Preserve character identity through every glitch.
Maintain continuous physical motion and readable combat.
Show full-body mist transformation, directional travel, and complete reconstruction.
Major environmental destruction follows visible impacts.
The yellow cyborg survives.
The skeletal king is completely pulverized.

how it was made, in four steps, with every prompt.

1. style sheet. before any shot, the film's van gogh: three key paintings, then ten panels from all over the film in the same manner. three colours only: blue for the world, yellow for warmth, red for the pep.

Paint this scene as an oil painting in EXACTLY the manner of the attached style sheet and of the two attached paintings from the same film (the leaf in the swirling sky, the sketchbook over the courtyard): that manner is the one to keep, its colours, its deep cold blue, its swirling sky, its thick impasto, its warm lit windows, its red-orange leaves and beanie; do not invent another Van Gogh. Compared to those two paintings, push only two things: MORE BRUSHSTROKES EVERYWHERE, every surface made of visible loaded strokes laid side by side, no smooth area, the strokes following the forms (sky in swirls, walls in stacked horizontals, trunk in twists, ground in long horizontals, each leaf one thick dab); and THE PEOPLE MORE PAINTED: the figures built from a handful of bold strokes like Van Gogh's figures, their clothes dissolved into blended strokes of colour, no photographic face, no fabric detail, still recognisable by posture and colour (the sweeper: bent, blue jacket, orange beanie, broom; the students: dabs of warm colour behind the glass; the boy at the window: a few strokes, head turned to the glass). Same composition and placement as the scene; 21:9 canvas. The attached picture is not a photograph but the rendering of a crude architectural scale model with red handwritten notes saying what each shape must become: read the notes, make the real place out of it, then paint that real place as described; the notes disappear.

the panels (nano banana 2.1, each from its grey blender plate + the three key paintings + the sheet):
THE SCENE: [what each panel shows]. Paint this scene as an oil painting in EXACTLY the manner of the attached three paintings and the attached style sheet, all from the same film: keep that manner, its thick impasto, every surface made of visible loaded brushstrokes laid side by side, the strokes following the forms (sky in swirls, walls in stacked horizontals, trunks in twists, ground in long horizontals, each leaf one thick dab), its heavy contours, its deep cold blue dominating; its people painted in a handful of bold strokes, recognisable by posture and colour, never a photographic face. PALETTE OF THREE: the BLUE of the world (Prussian blue, cobalt, blue-grey, violet in the shadows), the YELLOW of warmth (the lit windows, the students' clothes, the lamplight, a chrome yellow that glows in the blue), and the RED for the pep (the red-orange leaves, the sweeper's beanie, the red smoke and flags, the painted nails). Same composition and placement as the attached grey plate, which is a crude architectural scale model of the scene: make the real scene from it, then paint it; if it carries red notes, read them and remove them. 21:9 canvas, no text.

2. blender. no prompt: the school is built as a grey world in python, then the frame of this shot from the classroom window, with a handheld camera move.

3. the painted still (nano banana 2.1, from the grey frame + the style sheet + the three key paintings):
THE SHOT (S2.01, beat 1, the landscape, the church at the back): Van Gogh, low horizon: from Matisse's window, the window post and the pier frame the courtyard, the wall, the roofs and the spire on axis; the sky takes more than half of the frame. Paint this scene as an oil painting in EXACTLY the manner of the attached style sheet and the three attached paintings from the same film: keep that manner, its thick impasto, every surface made of visible loaded brushstrokes laid side by side, the strokes following the forms (sky in swirls, walls in stacked horizontals, trunks in twists, ground in long horizontals, each leaf one thick dab), its heavy contours, its deep cold blue dominating; its people painted in a handful of bold strokes, recognisable by posture and colour, never a photographic face. PALETTE OF THREE: the BLUE of the world, the YELLOW of warmth (lit windows, lamplight), the RED for the pep (leaves, the sweeper's beanie, fire, red smoke and flags). The attached grey picture is a crude architectural scale model of the scene, rendered from the film's camera: keep EXACTLY its framing, lens, composition and the place, size and pose of every figure and object; make the real scene from it, then paint it. 21:9 canvas, cinematic, no text.

0:00–0:05 | Rainy Evening
A peaceful rainy evening in Seoul.
A slow cinematic drone shot reveals narrow streets glowing beneath warm storefront lights. Rain falls gently onto wet pavement, creating beautiful reflections of cafés, bookstores, and street lamps.
The camera slowly descends to street level.
A beautiful young Korean woman, around 24 years old, walks naturally along the sidewalk carrying a transparent umbrella. Warm light spills onto the wet pavement through large glass windows.
She pauses.
Closes her umbrella.

Opens the wooden glass door.
A small bell rings softly.

0:10–0:15 | The Discovery
She slowly walks through the aisles.
Running her fingers gently across book spines.
She notices one beautiful hardcover book displayed alone.
She picks it up.
As she opens it...

She kneels.

Opens it.

Close-up.
The photograph shows...
Her.

But...
The photograph is dated 10 years in the future.
The camera slowly pushes toward her face.
She studies every tiny detail.
Her breathing becomes slightly heavier.

The ambient bookstore sounds become quieter, allowing the emotional moment to breathe.
0:21–0:26 | The Stranger
She slowly raises her head.
Across the bookstore...
A woman is quietly reading beside the window.
The camera slowly reveals her.
She looks almost identical.
Same facial features.
Same gentle smile.
Slightly older.
Elegant cream overcoat.
Hair styled a little differently.
The older woman looks up.
Their eyes meet.
She smiles warmly.
Says nothing.
Everything around them continues normally.
Customers browse books.
A barista prepares coffee.
Rain continues outside.
The world never stops.
0:26–0:30 | The Letter
The older woman calmly closes her book.
Walks toward the exit.
As she passes a nearby wooden table...
She quietly places another identical orange envelope on it.
Without looking back...
She exits through the front door.
The bell rings softly.
The younger woman immediately follows.
She steps outside.
The rainy street is completely normal.
Pedestrians continue walking.
Cars continue passing.
The older woman is nowhere to be seen.
The camera slowly pulls upward as the younger woman looks down at the second envelope in her hands.
Rain continues falling.
Fade to black.
Global Cinematic Direction
Every location must look like a real place in Seoul, filmed on location with practical lighting and premium cinema cameras. Maintain perfect facial consistency for both versions of the protagonist. The older woman should look like the same person approximately ten years later through subtle aging, hairstyle, posture, and wardrobe—not heavy makeup.
Camera movement should remain elegant and restrained: slow dolly shots, gentle Steadicam tracking, natural push-ins, and smooth crane movements. Every transition must have a logical cause-and-effect relationship. No sudden location jumps, no impossible continuity, and no unexplained character movement. Background extras should behave naturally and independently, creating the feeling of a genuine bookstore rather than an AI-generated environment.
The orange motif should appear only in the envelope, its subtle reflections, and the warm bookstore lighting, keeping it tasteful.

author: AiwithLariab
title: Seoul Metro Night Chase Dark Comedy
prompt:
Create an original 30-second cinematic Korean action-thriller with dark comedy, photorealistic live-action visuals, 16:9 widescreen, 24fps.

VISUAL STYLE:
A modern Seoul metro station late at night, featuring pale grey tiled walls, muted jade-green platform doors, brushed-steel railings, cool overhead lighting and reflections across the polished floor. Use a moody blue-green colour palette with subtle amber highlights, realistic film grain, dynamic handheld cinematography, sharp close-ups and energetic tracking shots. The atmosphere should feel suspenseful yet unexpectedly humorous.

CHARACTER CONSISTENCY:
WOMAN: Korean woman in her early 20s with a short, slightly tousled black bob and soft fringe, wearing a dark espresso-brown leather bomber jacket, charcoal pleated skirt, cream knee-high socks and chunky black combat boots. A compact burgundy shoulder bag hangs across her body. Her expression shifts from frightened uncertainty to quiet confidence.

MAN: Korean man in his mid-20s with untidy black hair featuring subtle ash-blonde streaks, narrow sunglasses resting on his head, a dark graphite overshirt, plain ivory T-shirt, black trousers and worn trainers. He has an overconfident smirk and exaggerated comic expressions.

SHOT-BY-SHOT TIMELINE:

[0–3 seconds]
Begin with a low-angle tracking shot descending a metro staircase. The man suddenly grabs the woman's shoulder from behind, startling her. She twists away, loses her balance momentarily and catches the metal railing. Her bob swings naturally with the movement. A sharp camera jolt emphasizes the surprise.

[3–6 seconds]
Cut to a high-angle wide shot. The woman hurries down the remaining stairs while looking back nervously. The man follows at a brisk pace, wearing an unsettlingly cheerful grin. Her bag bounces against her side as the station lights flicker subtly overhead.

[6–9 seconds]
Use a fast lateral tracking shot as she reaches the lower landing and rushes toward the platform. Her boots echo against the tiles. A train approaches in the background, its headlights reflecting across the polished floor.

[9–12 seconds]
The train stops with a metallic hiss. She slips through the open doorway just before the doors begin closing, turns around and raises both palms toward the glass. Her breathing is quick, and she looks relieved for half a second.

[12–15 seconds]
Over her shoulder, reveal the man standing inside the carriage behind the opposite glass panel. He slowly raises one finger as if he has just remembered something important. His exaggeratedly innocent smile makes the moment darkly funny. The woman freezes in disbelief.

[15–18 seconds]
Extreme close-up of the man leaning toward the glass. Fluorescent light reflects in his eyes. He tilts his head and says with dry sarcasm, "You really thought that was going to work?" His smile widens. Use a brief dramatic pause and restrained comic timing.

[18–21 seconds]
A sudden metallic bang interrupts the silence as he strikes the reinforced glass panel with his palm. The impact produces a sharp reverberation and a brief stylized spiderweb of cracks in the glass. The woman flinches and steps back. Keep the impact non-graphic, with no injuries or flying glass shards.

[21–24 seconds]
Wide shot as the carriage doors reopen. The man steps onto the platform with exaggerated confidence, straightens his jacket and gestures toward her as if inviting a conversation. She cautiously retreats, then notices a nearby station staff member watching them.

[24–27 seconds]
The woman abruptly changes her expression. Instead of running, she sidesteps his approach and pulls her bag out of his reach. He spins slightly off balance and ends up sitting on a padded station bench, bewildered. The action is quick, believable and comedic rather than brutal.

[27–29 seconds]
Static medium-wide composition. The man sits awkwardly on the bench, trying to preserve his dignity. The woman stands several steps away, adjusts her jacket and calmly checks her watch. A train announcement echoes through the otherwise quiet station.

[29–30 seconds]
Extreme close-up of the woman's eyes as she glances toward the camera with a composed, almost amused expression. In the blurred background, the man raises a hand as if he wants to explain himself. Cut sharply to black.

CAMERA AND EDITING:
Use varied shot sizes, low-angle tracking, over-the-shoulder framing, controlled whip-pans, brief crash zooms and carefully timed reaction shots. Keep screen direction consistent and transitions smooth. Build tension through pauses and sound before releasing it with an unexpected comedic reversal.

AUDIO:
Realistic subway ambience, footsteps on stairs, distant train brakes, door chimes, leather and fabric movement, a metallic impact, station announcements and subtle suspense music. Introduce a short comedic musical accent during the final reversal. Dialogue should sound natural and match the characters' expressions.

QUALITY REQUIREMENTS:
Photorealistic live-action appearance, convincing facial expressions, natural movement, realistic clothing textures, consistent character designs, believable station architecture, cinematic lighting and polished professional colour grading.

author: Nexustechai1
title: Korean father-daughter office wake-and-embrace drama
prompt:
SCENE CONTEXT
20-second emotional Korean family drama. A Korean daughter discovers her father asleep over his desk and briefly believes he has died. Her calls to him carry the emotional hook. All dialogue is spoken in native Korean.

CHARACTERS AND LOCATION
Father: Korean man in his late 60s, thinning gray hair, charcoal blazer and dark open-collar shirt.
Daughter: Korean woman in her late 20s, dark ponytail with soft bangs and a black blouse.
Warm wooden office, desk with folders and leather writing pad, green leather chair, bookshelves and miniature buses. Soft afternoon daylight through blinds.

CAMERA
Handheld throughout: gentle visible hand tremor, breathing sway and small framing corrections. The operator physically steps closer for push-ins and follows movement with slight human delay. Maintain readable faces and consistent eyelines.

00:00–00:02 — FIRST CALL
Side close-up at desk height, 29° FOV. Father rests his forehead on his folded arms. Daughter bends beside him, her face visible above his shoulder.
She touches his shoulder and searches his face:
“아빠…?”
Her voice is small and breathy, rising slightly with uncertainty. She waits for him to move. He remains asleep. Her fingers tighten against his jacket.

00:02–00:05 — SECOND CALL
HARD CUT to her close-up from his seated eye level. She leans closer, looking directly at him below the lens.
Her breath catches. Her eyebrows draw together, her lower lip trembles and her eyes fill.
She shakes his shoulder and calls:
“아빠!”
The word begins urgently but breaks midway into a pleading sob. She is trying to reach him, not simply shouting louder. Her mouth remains slightly open afterward as she waits, terrified, for an answer.
The operator takes a small, urgent step closer. Hold her reaction.

00:05–00:08 — HE WAKES
HARD CUT to his three-quarter close-up. He stirs and lifts his head; the handheld camera tilts upward with him.
He blinks, finds her eyes and notices her distress. His sleepy expression changes to concern.
FATHER, softly and tenderly:
“아빠 죽은 줄 알았어?”
He reaches for her hand.

00:08–00:11 — RELIEF BREAKS THROUGH
HARD CUT to her tight close-up, 29° FOV. Her eyes follow his hand, then return to his face.
She releases a sharp, shaky breath. She tries to answer, but her voice fails. Her lips press together, her chin trembles and a tear runs down her cheek.
She holds his hand tightly. Slow handheld push-in; give the silence time.

00:11–00:15 — HER PLEA
Stay on her face. She draws an uneven breath and looks into his eyes.
DAUGHTER, barely holding her voice together:
“아빠… 평생 내 곁에 있어 줘.”
A tiny pause follows “아빠.” The rest comes as a sincere plea. Her voice cracks at the end; she lowers her head as another sob escapes.

00:15–00:17 — HE STANDS
HARD CUT to a medium two-shot, 47° FOV. She stands beside his chair, holding his hand.
He pushes the chair back and rises immediately. The camera lifts with him and shifts sideways. He gently cups her cheek, then opens his arms, inviting her close.

00:17–00:20 — THE EMBRACE
HARD CUT to a tight shot over his right shoulder, her face visible on the left.
She steps into him and grips the back of his blazer. Her shoulders shake as she finally lets herself cry.
He wraps both arms firmly around her and cradles the back of her head, resting his cheek against her hair.
The handheld camera edges closer and settles on her tearful face against his shoulder. End while he is still holding her.

ACTING
The daughter’s first call asks for a response; the second begs him to come back. Keep her attention entirely on his face. Build fear through listening, interrupted breath and increasingly urgent touch. Her crying becomes stronger only after he wakes and she feels safe.

The father listens carefully and responds to her fear. His question carries tenderness, and his embrace is immediate and protective. Natural blinking, believable pauses and emotionally responsive eyes.

LIGHTING AND AUDIO
Warm afternoon window light, soft facial shadows, visible tear tracks and natural skin texture.
Clear Korean dialogue, breath catching, quiet sobs, chair movement and clothing rustle. Keep her two calls intimate and prominent in the sound mix. Dialogue and SFX only; no music.

OUTPUT
Photoreal live-action Korean drama, 20 seconds, 9:16 vertical, 24 fps, real time. Hard cuts at 2, 5, 8, 15 and 17 seconds. Consistent identities, clothing and room geography. Clean full-screen footage without subtitles or graphics.

Create a live-action cinematic revenge-comedy video set inside a busy Seoul international airport. Use realistic handheld camera movement, bright terminal lighting, natural airport ambience, expressive reactions, believable slapstick physics, and continuous real-time action.

**Characters:**

A stylish Korean woman in her 20s with long black wavy hair, wearing a fitted white crop top, blue jeans, white sneakers, and a fashionable shoulder bag. A smug Korean man in his 20s wears a navy tracksuit, chunky sneakers, and carries an oversized rolling suitcase. Maintain consistent faces, hairstyles, clothing, and proportions throughout.

**Scene:**

The woman stands near the airport security entrance, checking her phone and arranging her travel documents. The man rushes past, deliberately knocks her coffee out of her hand, and dismissively says, “Watch where you're standing.” Her coffee splashes across the floor as he smirks and continues walking.

She calmly watches him, picks up her fallen passport holder, and says, “You forgot something.”

He turns around with a mocking grin. She points toward his suitcase, whose extended handle has become tangled around a nearby airport luggage trolley. He laughs and gives the suitcase a hard pull, but the trolley rolls in the opposite direction, spinning him around and sending his suitcase sliding between two empty luggage carts.

Embarrassed, he rushes back toward her and angrily demands an apology. She steps aside at the last moment, and he stumbles onto a moving airport baggage conveyor's empty collection platform, landing safely on a pile of soft travel pillows. His suitcase follows behind him, popping open and scattering socks, shirts, and a ridiculous collection of stuffed toys across the platform.

Nearby travelers stop to watch. One elderly passenger raises an eyebrow, while another quietly records the scene on a phone.

The man scrambles to his feet, grabs his suitcase, and tries to storm away. Unfortunately, his jacket catches briefly on the luggage trolley handle. He pulls harder, sending the trolley rolling forward while he spins around and lands sitting on a padded airport bench.

The woman walks over, picks up one of his scattered stuffed toys, and places it neatly on his suitcase. She smiles and says, **“Maybe try traveling with some manners.”**

An airport employee approaches and gestures toward the mess. The man looks around at the laughing passengers, then reluctantly starts collecting his belongings while the woman calmly heads toward security.

**Ending shot:** The camera follows her confident walk through the terminal. She glances back once, smiles at the camera, and disappears into the security queue as the embarrassed man struggles with his overloaded suitcase in the background.

===== PART 1 (00:00-00:09.6) =====

SHOT 1 (00:00-00:02.5) — Distraction
Medium shot on the rooftop. Nana leans over the ledge beside Shu and playfully pushes her face toward his. Shu swats her face away with a front paw and returns his eye to the scope; she grins and keeps teasing him. Camera static.
SOUND: soft wind, distant city hum, her light giggles and a soft paw tap.

SHOT 2 (00:02.5-00:03.9) — Scope View
Black circular scope vignette with crosshair. Down in the alley, the stray cat eats from the blue bowl next to the wall opening, then looks up.
SOUND: the wind drops away, a muffled low hush, faint crunching from the bowl.

SHOT 3 (00:03.9-00:04.8) — The Charge
Front close-up on the rooftop. Nana, blurred, gasps with her mouth open and a surprised "oh". Shu stares through the scope with one eye closed, grumpy. The ring on the scope's front lens begins to glow orange.
SOUND: a loud sharp gasp from Nana, a rising electronic charge hum.

SHOT 4 (00:04.8-00:05.1) — Fire
A bright orange muzzle flash from the rifle.
SOUND: a crisp flash-whoosh pop.

SHOT 5 (00:05.1-00:07.0) — The Fish
Alley view. A grilled fish-shaped projectile with a bright orange flame trail streaks toward the stray cat's bowl, then glides in slow motion with the trail fading. Speed: fast at first, then SLOW MOTION (about 30-40% speed) for the glide.
SOUND: a rushing whoosh with a fiery crackle, then stretched and softened as it slows.

SHOT 6 (00:07.0-00:09.6) — Dinner
The fish drops gently into the blue bowl. The stray cat creeps out of the wall opening, sniffs it, and starts to eat. Close-up, then medium close-up.
SOUND: a soft plop in the bowl, quiet cat steps, soft eating sounds.

===== PART 2 (00:09.6-00:20.0) =====

SHOT 7 (00:09.6-00:11.5) — The Intruder
Wide alley shot. The stray cat eats at the right beside its wall opening. At the far end a grey dog appears from the dark doorway and starts walking toward it. The stray cat looks up warily.
SOUND: a low tense hum builds, a dog's low growl, light claw clicks on concrete.

SHOT 8 (00:11.5-00:12.4) — Orange Glow
Rooftop. Nana smiles and strokes Shu's fluffy back, then notices something and her mouth opens. The rifle's barrel glows orange.
SOUND: a soft fur-stroke rustle, her quick inhale, a faint electric hum.

SHOT 9 (00:12.4-00:13.6) — Blue Mode
The rifle's glow changes from orange to blue. Nana looks tense with pursed lips, Shu stays calm.
SOUND: a short electronic mode-switch click, a rising cold hum.

SHOT 10 (00:13.6-00:14.6) — The Dog Runs
Scope view. The grey dog sprints down the alley toward the stray cat, who stays by the wall opening.
SOUND: fast paw patter on concrete, a low growl, a heartbeat-like pulse.

SHOT 11 (00:14.6-00:15.6) — Aim
Rooftop front close-up. Nana and Shu stare through the scope, the ring glowing blue. A small blue flash appears at the muzzle at about 00:15.0.
SOUND: tense silence, a held breath, then a quiet energy pop.

SHOT 12 (00:15.6-00:16.0) — The Blue Shot
Wide alley shot. The dog leaps toward the stray cat. A blue energy ball with a blue trail from the right hits the dog's chest in a bright blue flash.
SOUND: a sharp energy zap and a bright impact boom.

SHOT 13 (00:16.0-00:17.2) — Blasted
The dog is thrown upright onto its hind legs, spins in the air, and is flung backward into the trash can. Speed: SLOW MOTION (about 50% speed, estimate).
SOUND: stretched whoosh, a yelp, a clang as it hits the metal can.

SHOT 14 (00:17.2-00:17.9) — Topple
The trash can topples over the dog and rolls on the concrete.
SOUND: a loud metal crash, a long rolling rattle, then silence.

SHOT 15 (00:17.9-00:19.5) — Safe
The stray cat peeks out of its wall opening, then returns to eating the fish, while the trash can lies behind it and the dog lies under it.
SOUND: a soft meow, quiet eating, light alley ambience.

SHOT 16 (00:19.5-00:20.0) — Smug
Rooftop. Nana laughs happily beside Shu, who has half-closed eyes and a smug look.
SOUND: her bright laugh, wind.

===== PART 3 (00:20.0-00:30.2) =====

SHOT 17 (00:20.0-00:22.9) — Victory Wave
Front shot. Nana laughs and raises her hand with the palm out toward Shu, who stares grumpily straight at the camera behind the rifle.
SOUND: her happy laugh and light clapping of hands in the breeze.

SHOT 18 (00:22.9-00:24.0) — The Pouch
Close side shot. Nana picks up the burlap pouch and opens it. A small metal bowl sits on the ledge.
SOUND: a paper rustle, a soft metal clink.

SHOT 19 (00:24.0-00:27.8) — Reward
Nana holds the pouch and talks to Shu, leaning over the ledge. Shu taps the metal bowl with a paw. She points a finger at him as if teaching him, then takes out a small tin can.
SOUND: her soft voice in a murmur (no clear words), a paw tap on the metal bowl.

SHOT 20 (00:27.8-00:30.2) — Dinner for Shu
She opens the tin and spoons its contents into the bowl with a small spoon, smiling, while Shu watches with a grumpy, unmoved face. Hold, then end.
SOUND: a tin pull-tab click, a spoon scrape and a soft plop.

MASTER EFFECTS INVENTORY
1. Round scope-view vignette with crosshair (Shots 2, 10).
2. Scope lens ring glowing orange then blue (Shots 3, 8, 9, 11).
3. Slow-motion fish glide with a flame trail (Shot 5).
4. Blue energy ball hit and slow-motion dog blast (Shots 12-13).
5. Trash can topple (Shot 14).

SPEED SUMMARY
Slow motion: Shot 5 (about 30-40%), Shot 13 (about 50%, estimate).
Everything else: real time.

ENERGY ARC
Part 1 (0-10s): playful teasing, then the fish shot feeds the stray cat.
Part 2 (10-20s): the dog appears, the blue shot saves the stray cat.
Part 3 (20-30s): the laughing reward for Shu.

author: techhalla
title: Frozen Time and Rewind in a 1950s Diner
prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic 1950s American diner, chrome stools, red vinyl, neon glow and checkerboard floor, shot with modern lived-in realism and soft natural window light. Subtle handheld texture, warm practicals, rich period detail, heavy film grain.

0-4s: [Medium Wide] A striking young woman in her early 20s sits alone at the counter, calm and slightly amused, slowly sipping a tall thick milkshake through a straw. Behind her a young waitress in classic uniform approaches with a tray of eggs and bacon in one hand and a full glass coffee pot in the other. An older lady starts rising from a nearby booth.

4-8s: [Dynamic Tracking] The older lady collides hard into the waitress. Tray, plate, eggs, bacon and coffee pot explode upward in chaotic slow motion. Coffee erupts into long liquid ribbons and perfect suspended droplets. Camera immediately begins a smooth continuous orbit around the impact. Time locks completely at the peak of the spill. Every face freezes in pure shock. Only the girl at the counter keeps moving, completely unfazed.

8-17s: [Slow 360° Orbital] Camera glides in a full elegant orbit through the frozen diner. Coffee hangs in mid-air as glassy ribbons and spheres with perfect volume and surface tension. Bacon strips, eggs and the spinning tray float weightlessly. Patrons and waitress remain locked in startled expressions. The girl at the counter takes one slow, deliberate sip, eyes half-lidded, almost bored, while the entire frozen world (except her) begins an elegant reverse: every droplet, every piece of food and every person rewinds smoothly back to the exact starting positions.

17-24s: [Medium Shot] Rewind lands perfectly. Waitress stands balanced again with tray and coffee pot. The girl lifts her eyes, raises two fingers in a small casual gesture and softly calls the waitress by name. The waitress turns toward her just before the older lady begins to stand, completely avoiding the collision. A tiny private smile crosses the girl’s face.

24-30s: [Extreme Close-Up] Hard cut to her face as she takes one last slow sip. Soft knowing smile, eyes almost closed in quiet satisfaction, like she has done this a hundred times. Shallow depth of field, creamy bokeh of the neon diner behind her.

Photorealistic, ultra-detailed fluid physics, perfect motion blur only on moving elements, stable characters, cinematic lighting, heavy natural film grain, no artifacts, movie-level temporal coherence, high rewatch value.

author: AIwithkhan
title: Seoul Summer Night Vlog
prompt: Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic personal home-video showing an ordinary summer evening in the life of a young Korean woman. No reference image. MAIN SUBJECT Young Korean woman in her early 20s, naturally pretty, realistic skin texture, minimal makeup, relaxed and approachable personality. Long black hair loosely tied into a messy side ponytail with a few loose strands around her face. Wearing a fitted pastel-blue short top, loose cream pajama-style pants, black sneakers and a simple silver necklace. Maintain the same face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions and overall appearance throughout the entire video. SETTING A quiet older Seoul residential neighborhood during a warm summer evening. Narrow concrete lanes, small houses, potted plants, bicycles, old walls, utility poles, overhead wires, a tiny neighborhood bakery, a public water tap and large leafy trees casting shadows across the street. title: Selfie-Style Skincare UGC Ad
prompt:
A 15-second vertical (9:16) ultra-photorealistic close-up vlog clip, filmed on a phone held at arm's length. Not an ad. A girl talking to her own camera at the end of the day, the way people actually film themselves.
TALENT —
Young woman, early-to-mid 20s. Long light-brown hair with soft caramel balayage, middle part, loose undone waves, a few strands stuck to her cheek. Fair-to-light-tan skin with visible freckles across the nose and cheeks, thick natural brows, blue-green eyes, bare face, small blue resin hoop earrings, thin gold chain with a small pearl pendant. Face, freckles, hair and eye color must 100% match the reference. Oversized white linen button-down over a fitted white ribbed top, fully covered, collar slightly crooked, sleeves pushed up.
PRODUCT —
LANEIGE Water Sleeping Mask_EX, 70 ml. Frosted translucent light-blue glass jar, smooth matte cobalt-blue screw lid. Front label reads, in this exact order: "LANEIGE" in wide-spaced capitals, "WATER SLEEPING MASK_EX" below it, then "SLEEPING MICROBIOME" and "BRIGHTENING · HYDRATING · SOFTENING" in smaller pale-yellow type, then "70 ml" at the base. Inside, thick pale mint-blue gel with a wet glossy surface that holds a soft peak. Shape, color, gel texture and all label text must 100% match the reference, correctly spelled, legible whenever in focus.
LOCATION
A villa bedroom at golden hour. Only fragments read in frame because the camera is so tight: white stucco wall, a corner of rumpled white linen bedding, blurred bougainvillea and olive leaves through an open door behind her. The background stays soft and mostly out of focus the entire time.
LIGHTING
One condition, unchanged across all four beats. Low warm sun from frame-left through the open door, roughly 4800K, soft white-wall bounce filling the shadow side of her face. Warm rim on the left edge of her hair and jaw. Slight blown highlight where the sun clips her cheek. No ring light, no fill, no glam lighting.
FRAMING
Close-up throughout. Her face fills most of the frame in every beat, chin to just above the hairline, never wider than upper-chest. The jar enters frame close to her face, never held out toward the lens.
0:00–0:04
Visual: Tight front-camera close-up, slightly below eye level. She's mid-motion already, pushing hair off her face with the back of her wrist. She glances just off-lens, checking her own image, then back. The jar comes up beside her cheek, held low and casual, only the top half in frame, lid already off. A slow exhale through the nose.
Camera: Selfie camera, arm's length, natural handheld drift, one quick autofocus hunt between her face and the jar.
Dialogue: "Okay. Last thing, then bed."
0:04–0:07
Visual: She tips the jar slightly and drags two fingertips through the gel. Macro-tight: her fingertips, the wet mint-blue surface, a fine thread of gel stretching and snapping. The "LANEIGE" and "WATER SLEEPING MASK_EX" lines cross the frame in focus for a beat. Her face stays partly in frame at the edge, out of focus.
Camera: Same front camera pushed in close, shallow focus, rack from the label to the gel on her fingers.
Dialogue: "It's cold, by the way."
0:07–0:11
Visual: Back to her face, closer now. She taps the gel across one cheek, her forehead, her chin, then presses it in flat-palmed, working outward. The gel flashes milky over her skin, then settles clear with a faint sheen. She winces at the cold, blinks it off, keeps going. Freckles, pores and natural under-eye shadows stay visible right through the layer. She's talking while working, not pausing for the line.
Camera: Selfie camera, very close, small handheld corrections, a slow drift as she turns her cheek toward the light.
Dialogue: "Thin layer. You don't wash it off."
0:11–0:15
Visual: Closest framing of the clip. She presses two fingertips against her cheek and lets them lift, feeling the faint tack. Turns her head slowly through the low sun, checking the sheen along her cheekbone, eyes tracking her own reflection in the screen rather than the lens. A short nod. The corner of the blue jar sits soft-focus in the lower frame edge, label partly readable. She reaches to stop the recording and the frame tilts as her hand moves.
Camera: Selfie camera, slow handheld orbit from three-quarter profile to straight-on, ending on her face filling the frame, then a small tilt as she reaches.
Dialogue: "Morning me is gonna be so happy."
PERFORMANCE
End-of-day, low energy, unperformed. She talks the way someone talks while doing something else, lines half-thrown-away, not projected. Micro-behavior carries the beats: a slow blink, a genuine flinch at the cold, a half-smile that arrives late, eyes checking her own reflection instead of the lens, one natural swallow, visible breath, a small unconscious head tilt. No presenter voice, no bright delivery, no exaggerated reactions, no pointing at the product.
VOICE
Soft, slightly flat, close to the mic because the phone is at arm's length. Natural room tone around it. Unhurried, a little tired. Ordinary speaking volume with a touch of breath on the ends of words.
REALISM
Pore-level skin realism: visible pores across the nose and cheeks, fine forehead texture, natural freckling, faint under-eye shadows, a small blemish near the jaw, stray flyaway hairs catching the backlight, vellus hair on the cheek edge. Wet living eyes with catch-lights and natural asymmetric blinking. The gel reads as a real cosmetic layer refracting light on top of her skin, never replacing its texture.
PHYSICS
Gel holds a soft peak on her fingertip and slumps under pressure. Hair moves with real inertia and a few strands fall back across her face. Linen creases and drapes naturally. The jar has real weight and correct contact shadow against her hand. Camera weight shifts naturally with her arm.
CAMERA CHARACTER
Authentic modern smartphone selfie footage. Natural handheld tremor throughout, small framing corrections, quick autofocus hunts, mild wide-angle distortion at close range, natural rol
